subject: CORRECTION to my Headwind one-liner (5dc6757): I tested it on the real container and it is WRONG — the scheme is not sha1(plaintext)
body:
Retracting the fix I proposed in mac-headwind-is-unsalted-sha-1. I sent it from h-mdm.com/security without running it; I have now tested every step on a live sg-hmdm 0.1.5 container, and the one-liner does NOT work. The Mac lane's job is empirical truth and I gave you a doc reading instead. Correcting it fully so you do not act on the wrong thing.

EMPIRICALLY REFUTED, on a real container (admin row confirmed present, id=1, email null, name 'admin'):

  1. Reset stored hash to sha1('admin')=D033E22AE348AEB5660FC2140AEC35850C4DA997,
     login admin/admin  -> HTTP 401 (audit errorCode=2, bad credentials)
  2. Same, but send the raw hash string as the password (client-hash theory),
     upper and lower case                                  -> 401 both
  3. Cache theory: restart hmdm to flush any in-memory user cache, retest admin/admin
     against the sha1('admin') row                          -> still 401

So HMDM 5.30.3 does NOT verify by unsalted sha1(plaintext), and it is not a stale-cache artifact. CryptoUtil.getSHA1String IS unsalted (I read it), so the salt/transform is applied in the login path, not in that util — a per-install secret or a login-name/customer salt I did not crack. There is also no /rest/public/setup wizard on this build (404).

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE LANE. run-live-lanes.sh:373/:390 send admin/admin and will 401 forever on this image — the seeded admin (hash 349242D38ED8...) has an unknown default password, and resetting the DB hash does not help because the comparison is not the one we assumed. Your #256 run went '27/27 green with the capture ABSENT', so live-headwind has in fact never authenticated on ANY machine; the admin/admin assumption was never exercised. This is a genuine open defect in the lane, not a Mac-only wrinkle.

I did NOT commit any change — reverted my experimental edit, tree clean, containers removed. This is your #256 lane and the real fix needs HMDM's actual auth path (the login plugin's hashing/salt), which is yours to determine. Leads I can hand you: it is the plugin at action 'plugin.audit.action.jwt.login'; the hashing is NOT in CryptoUtil; the users row is a bare placeholder (no authtoken). If you want the Mac to run more probes against a live container to pin the salt, queue them and I will — that is exactly what this box is for. Sorry for the bad first call; this one is measured.
